labels.label: Appeal to Authority
labels.definition: A claim is treated as justified primarily because an authority or expert endorses it.
conditions: expertise or authority status is used as evidential support

labels.label: Appeal to Majority
labels.definition: A claim is treated as true or good primarily because many people accept or practice it.
conditions: majority acceptance or prevalence is used as evidential support

labels.label: Appeal to Nature
labels.definition: A claim is treated as good, right, or preferable primarily because it is described as natural.
conditions: natural status is used to infer value or correctness

labels.label: Appeal to Tradition
labels.definition: A practice or claim is defended primarily because it is traditional or longstanding.
conditions: historical persistence is used to infer correctness or value

labels.label: Appeal to Worse Problems
labels.definition: A concern is dismissed or deprioritized because a worse problem exists.
mechanisms: comparison to worse issue used to dismiss concern
conditions: relative severity replaces engagement with the focal issue

labels.label: False Dilemma
labels.definition: A limited set of alternatives is presented as exhaustive when other possibilities exist.
conditions: two or few options are presented as the only choices

labels.label: Hasty Generalization
labels.definition: A broad conclusion is drawn from an insufficient or unrepresentative sample.
mechanisms: limited sample generalized to broader scope
conditions: evidence scope is narrower than conclusion scope

labels.label: Slippery Slope
labels.definition: An initial action is claimed to lead through an insufficiently supported chain to an extreme consequence.
conditions: intermediate causal links are asserted without adequate support
